# Glossary and resources

## Glossary

Definitions here match the usage the chapters rely on, and each points at the
section where the term does its work. Where a definition rests on a published
source, that source is cited.

Ten entries carry no citation, in two different situations.

Four of them are the ones to look at first, marked in italics in place. For
these the absence of a defining source is itself a finding: the term is in use
and no paper establishes it. They are **intron chain**, **isoform fraction and
dIF**, **cassette exon** as a synonym for skipped exon, and the stated limits
of **event-level metrics**. Those four definitions are written on this book's
authority and need a reader's sign-off.

The remaining six are standard terms that no particular paper owns:
**colocalisation**, **microexon**, **poison exon**, **pseudoexon**, the **QTL**
family and **TPM**. They are given here as the book uses them, without
a citation, because attaching one would imply a provenance they do not have.

**Alternative polyadenylation (APA)**
: Choosing among a gene's several poly(A) sites, producing transcripts that
differ in 3' UTR, terminal exon or coding potential. An isoform-generating
process in its own right, with no splicing difference required
[@huang2026apacancer]. See @sec-ends.

**AS-NMD**
: Splicing that produces a transcript in order for decay to remove it, so that
the fraction of transcripts reaching protein is set after transcription. Also
published as regulated unproductive splicing and translation
[@garciamoreno2020asnmd]. See @sec-as-nmd.

**Cassette exon**
: An exon that is either included in or skipped from the mature transcript.
Used in this book as a synonym for skipped exon. *No source defines the two
terms as equivalent; this equivalence is the book's own and is flagged for
review.* The event class itself is one of the five named in
[@sammeth2008nomenclature]. See @sec-event-classes.

**Colocalisation**
: A test of whether a trait association and a molecular QTL at the same locus
are driven by the same causal variant, rather than by two variants in linkage
disequilibrium. See @sec-coloc-gap.

**Differential gene expression (DGE)**
: A test of whether a gene's total transcriptional output changed
[@soneson2016differential]. See @sec-dtu and @fig-dge-dtu-dte.

**Differential transcript expression (DTE)**
: A test of whether an individual transcript changed in abundance
[@soneson2016differential]. See @sec-dtu.

**Differential transcript usage (DTU)**
: A test of whether the composition of a gene's isoform abundance spectrum
changed, independently of its total [@soneson2016differential]. See @sec-dtu.

**Dominant transcript**
: A gene's major transcript, meaning the one with highest expression, when it is
expressed at considerably more than any minor one. Operationalised as at least
twice the abundance of the next [@gonzalezporta2013dominanttranscript]. See
@sec-scale.

**Event-level metric**
: Any measure that scores one splicing decision rather than solving for
full-length structure, PSI being the canonical case. *Its limits are stated
on the book's own authority and are flagged for review:* an event-level metric
cannot report which decisions co-occurred in the same molecule, and a single
value can average over two decisions taken independently
[@pervouchine2013introncentric]. See @sec-psi.

**Full splice match (FSM)**
: An observed transcript reproducing every splice junction of some reference
transcript. Says nothing about whether the ends agree
[@tardaguila2018sqanti]. See @sec-transcript-classes.

**Incomplete splice match (ISM)**
: An observed transcript reproducing a consecutive run of a reference
transcript's junctions but not all of them. Can be a genuinely shorter isoform
or a truncated cDNA [@tardaguila2018sqanti]. See @sec-transcript-classes.

**Intron chain**
: The ordered list of a transcript's internal intron coordinates. Two
transcripts match at intron-chain level when every intron has identical
coordinates and the counts agree, which implies that all internal exons match
and says nothing about the terminal boundaries
[@pertea2020gffutilities]. *The term is in wide use and no paper coins it; the
earliest operational definition located for this book is the one cited.
Flagged for review.* See @sec-transcript-classes and
[the comparison walkthrough](../walkthroughs/intron-chain-comparison.qmd).

**Intron retention**
: An intron present in a mature polyadenylated transcript. The one event class
whose observation does not establish that a splicing decision was taken, since
it is equally compatible with an unfinished intermediate
[@jacob2017intronretention]. See @sec-event-classes.

**Isoform**
: Any of the distinct transcripts a gene produces. Not a synonym for splice
variant, since alternative transcription start sites and alternative
polyadenylation generate isoforms without any splicing difference
[@carrion2023alternativetranscripts].

**Isoform fraction (IF), and dIF**
: The share of a gene's output carried by one of its isoforms, and the change in
that share between two conditions. *No source defines these terms; the
definitions here are the book's own and are flagged for review.* The quantity
is what differential transcript usage tests. See @sec-dtu.

**Microexon**
: An exon only a few to a few dozen bases long, so that including or excluding
it changes a short stretch of protein rather than a domain. Isoforms differing
by one are easily missed, both by short reads and by tools that assume exons are
longer. See @sec-rps24.

**MANE Select, MANE Plus Clinical**
: One representative transcript per human protein-coding gene, identical in exon
structure between Ensembl/GENCODE and RefSeq; and the additional set for loci
where pathogenic variants fall on exons the Select transcript omits
[@morales2022mane]. See @sec-mane.

**Minor spliceosome**
: The parallel U12-dependent machinery that excises a small fraction of introns,
recognising different signals from the major U2-dependent spliceosome
[@akinyi2021minorspliceosome]. See @sec-mechanism.

**Nonsense-mediated decay (NMD)**
: Degradation triggered when a stop codon sits far enough upstream of the last
exon junction to leave an exon junction complex downstream of it after the
first round of translation [@lindeboom2016nmdrules]. See @sec-as-nmd.

**Novel in catalog (NIC), novel not in catalog (NNC)**
: An observed transcript using only annotated splice sites in an unannotated
combination, and one introducing a splice site the annotation does not contain
[@tardaguila2018sqanti]. See @sec-transcript-classes.

**Percent spliced-in (PSI, Ψ)**
: The fraction of a gene's mRNAs containing a given exon, estimated from the
density of inclusion reads over the sum of inclusion and exclusion densities
[@wang2008alternative]. See @sec-psi.

**Poison exon**
: An alternative exon whose inclusion introduces a premature stop codon and
sends the transcript to decay. See @sec-cancer-therapeutics.

**Proteoform**
: A distinct molecular form of a protein produced from one gene. The term covers
differences arising from genetic variation, from splicing, and from
modification after translation, which this book otherwise treats separately
[@proteoformmedicine2026]. See @sec-measuring.

**Pseudoexon**
: An intronic sequence spliced into a transcript as though it were an exon,
usually because a variant created or strengthened a splice site. See
@sec-rnaseq-diagnosis.

**QTL: eQTL, sQTL, isoform QTL, apaQTL**
: A variant associated with a molecular phenotype, respectively gene-level
expression, a splicing event, an isoform's expression or usage, and poly(A)
site choice. See @sec-qtl-position and @sec-isoform-qtl.

**Splice chain, start site, end site**
: The three parts of a transcript that can vary independently. Annotation has
historically given one chain exactly one of each [@reese2023encode4]. See
@sec-three-axes.

**Top-down proteomics**
: Mass spectrometry performed on intact protein molecules rather than on
fragments of them. It is the approach that can report which combination of
features one molecule actually carries, which fragment-based measurement
cannot [@xu2024topdown]. See @sec-measuring.

**Transcripts per million (TPM)**
: A within-sample abundance unit, normalised for transcript length and then for
sequencing depth.

## What this book deliberately does not do

<!-- numbers-ok: the dates below describe the resources themselves, not
     claims drawn from papers, so they have no claim record to match. -->

This is a biology book. It does not catalogue software, benchmark tools, or teach
pipelines. That work is done well elsewhere, and duplicating it would both
waste effort and date the book quickly. What exists as of November 2026:

### Tool catalogues

<!-- numbers-ok: last-updated dates for the listed resources. -->

- [**long-read-tools.org**](https://long-read-tools.org/). Ritchie Lab (WEHI)
  catalogue of long-read analysis tools, including a transcriptomics category.
  Actively curated, accepts submissions.
- [**awesome-alternative-splicing**](https://github.com/HussainAther/awesome-alternative-splicing). A curated splicing tool list. Note it has not been updated since 2018 and
  predates the long-read era; useful mainly as a record of the short-read
  toolkit.

### Methods training

- [**rnabio.org**](https://rnabio.org/). Griffith Lab RNA-seq course, usable standalone, with a module on isoform analysis and assembly.
- [**EBI: Long-read RNA-seq analysis**](https://www.ebi.ac.uk/training/materials/introduction-to-rna-seq-materials/qc-dwnstream-analysis/long-read-rna-seq-analysis/). Part of EBI's *Introduction to RNA-seq and functional interpretation*.
- [**Galaxy Training Network: differential isoform expression**](https://training.galaxyproject.org/training-material/topics/transcriptomics/tutorials/differential-isoform-expression/tutorial.html). Hands-on isoform switching.

### Databases and knowledge bases

Where this book makes a biological case, these are where a reader goes to look up
a specific gene or isoform.

- [**APPRIS**](https://appris.bioinfo.cnio.es/). Principal isoform selection,
  plus annotation of known functional alternative isoforms.
- [**MANE**](https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/refseq/MANE/). Matched RefSeq/Ensembl
  representative transcripts; discussed critically in
  [the cataloguing chapter](09-catalogs.qmd).
- [**GENCODE**](https://www.gencodegenes.org/). Reference transcript annotation.
- **ASpdb**, **IsoProDB**, **SPLISOFORMS**. Protein-isoform-level knowledge
  bases integrating structure, domains, disorder and NMD annotation.
- [**isopedia**](https://github.com/zhengxinchang/isopedia). Read-level indexing
  across large numbers of long-read transcriptomes.

### Adjacent communities

<!-- numbers-ok: a renaming date for an organisation, not a sourced claim. -->

- [**Proteoform Alliance**](https://ctdp.org/) (formerly the Consortium for
  Top-Down Proteomics, renamed October 2026) and the
  [**Human Proteoform Project**](https://www.science.org/doi/10.1126/sciadv.abk0734). The same argument made one level down, at the protein level. Natural allies:
  a transcript isoform that is never translated into a distinct proteoform, and a
  proteoform with no transcript-level explanation, are each other's open
  questions.
